guide_enrichment.narrative:
What stands out to us is Missouri’s defensive path to controlling the game. Our numbers favor its pass defense against Mississippi State’s passing attack, and we also see a substantial advantage in preventing the Bulldogs from creating scoring opportunities. That gives Missouri a credible foundation, but the defense returned only two starters from 2025, so we are careful not to treat one strong matchup as certainty.

The counterweight is Missouri’s offense. The Tigers produced 562 yards in their opener, but that result is context rather than proof that the passing game will consistently create separation. Missouri returned only five offensive starters and replaced its quarterback and three starting receivers. Our numbers remain less convinced by this passing offense against Mississippi State’s pass defense, which helps explain why we are slightly more restrained than the market. The disagreement is simply not large enough for us at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: For us, the matchup to watch is Missouri’s passing game against Mississippi State’s pass defense. Austin Simmons is the new starter and completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in his Missouri debut. That was an encouraging first data point, but our model still views this as the area most likely to determine whether Missouri can create enough separation. If the opener carries over against a more demanding pass-defense matchup, Missouri’s ceiling rises; if not, the game becomes more compressed.

recent_game.fact: Missouri opened the 2026 season with a 54-14 win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Sept. 3.
Missouri produced 562 total yards against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, including 357 passing and 205 rushing, while allowing 198 total yards.
Missouri led Arkansas-Pine Bluff 40-0 at halftime and outgained the Golden Lions 376-6 in the first half.
Missouri converted 6 of 10 third downs, both fourth-down attempts and all five red-zone opportunities against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

opponent_notes.fact: Missouri is scheduled to play at Mississippi State on Sept. 26, 2026 in an SEC game.

quarterback.fact: Ole Miss transfer Austin Simmons is Missouri's starting quarterback, with sophomore Matt Zollers listed as the backup.
In his Missouri debut, Simmons completed 17 of 19 passes for 252 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
Simmons' 89.5% completion rate and 270.4 passer rating against Arkansas-Pine Bluff were the highest by a quarterback in his Missouri debut.
Simmons is the seventh different starting quarterback of the Eli Drinkwitz era and the third transfer quarterback to start during that span.

offensive_personnel.fact: Missouri's listed starting offensive line is LT Cayden Green, LG Tristan Wilson, C Dominick Giudice, RG Curtis Peagler and RT Luke Work.
Missouri returned five offensive starters from 2025 and lost six, including quarterback Beau Pribula, center Connor Tollison and three starting wide receivers.
The listed starting skill players are running back Jamal Roberts, tight end Brett Norfleet or Jordon Harris, and receivers Naeshaun Montgomery or Caleb Goodie Sr., Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode.
Ole Miss transfer Cayden Lee started at receiver in the opener and caught five passes for 89 yards, including a 47-yard touchdown from former Ole Miss teammate Austin Simmons.
Donovan Olugbode set career highs with seven receptions, 107 yards and two touchdowns in the opener.
Jamal Roberts led Missouri with 13 carries for 47 yards and one touchdown in the opener and surpassed 1,000 career rushing yards.

defensive_personnel.fact: Missouri returned two defensive starters from 2025 and lost 10, including defensive end Zion Young, linebacker Josiah Trotter, defensive tackle Chris McClellan and cornerbacks Toriano Pride Jr. and Drey Norwood.
Transfer linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr. and transfer cornerback Chris Graves Jr. are listed as starters on Missouri's 2026 defense.
Woodyard started 11 games for Auburn in 2025 and recorded 67 tackles, including 50 in conference play.
Graves appeared in 41 games over three seasons at Ole Miss and started nine games in 2025.
Missouri's listed defensive front consists of Langden Kitchen, Marquis Gracial, Jalen Marshall and Darris Smith, with Nicholas Rodriguez and Robert Woodyard Jr. at linebacker.

coaching_changes.fact: Chip Lindsey joined Missouri as offensive coordinator in December 2025 and is in his first season with the Tigers.
Garrett Riley joined Missouri in January 2026 as quarterbacks coach after serving as Clemson's offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
John Papuchis was named Missouri's special-teams coordinator and defensive assistant in January 2026.
Derek Nicholson added co-defensive coordinator duties before the 2026 season while continuing to coach linebackers.

offensive_context.fact: Missouri averaged 228.3 rushing yards per game in 2025 and recorded a program-record 12 individual 100-yard rushing performances.
Missouri rushed for 31 touchdowns in 2025 and scored three rushing touchdowns in its 2026 opener.
Against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, Missouri averaged 7.2 yards per play, converted 60% of its third downs and scored touchdowns on four of five red-zone possessions.

defensive_context.fact: Missouri's 2025 defense allowed 277.3 yards and 18.9 points per game, including 103.8 rushing yards and 173.5 passing yards per game.
Missouri held Arkansas-Pine Bluff to 198 total yards, 89 rushing yards, 109 passing yards and a 3-of-13 third-down conversion rate.
Missouri's defense forced five three-and-outs against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.

special_teams.fact: Blake Craig remains Missouri's starting placekicker, while Florida State transfer Brunno Reus is listed as the starting punter, holder and kickoff specialist.
Craig made a 32-yard field goal and all seven extra-point attempts against Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
DaMarion Fowlkes is listed as Missouri's primary punt and kickoff returner.

series_context.fact: Missouri defeated Mississippi State 49-27 in Columbia on Nov. 15, 2025.
Ahmad Hardy rushed for 300 yards and three touchdowns against Mississippi State in the 2025 meeting.
Darris Smith recorded three tackles for loss against Mississippi State in 2025.

other_relevant.fact: Missouri entered 2026 with five returning offensive starters, two returning defensive starters and two returning special-teams starters.
